ADMISSION NOTE
Ward: Trauma & Orthopaedics
Admitted: 29/07/2026 19:00
Clerked by: FY2 in Trauma & Orthopaedics

Patient: Kirsty Davies
DOB: 13/01/1948 (78y)   Sex: Female
Hospital no: 8944911

PRESENTING COMPLAINT
Pain and deformity of the right wrist following a fall at home.

HISTORY OF PRESENTING COMPLAINT
78y female brought to ED at 17:25 after a mechanical fall from standing height onto outstretched hand at
approximately 16:50 today. Tripped on a rug indoors, fell forwards,
put the right hand out to save herself. Immediate pain and obvious deformity of the
right wrist, unable to use the arm since. No loss of consciousness, no head strike,
no preceding dizziness, chest pain or palpitations - a mechanical fall. No other injury;
no neck or back pain, no other limb pain, able to weight-bear normally. Denies numbness or
tingling in the hand at any point. Right-hand dominant.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension; hypothyroidism; osteoarthritis of both knees. No previous fragility fracture. No previous surgery to
this limb.

DRUG HISTORY
Amlodipine 5mg OD; atorvastatin 20mg ON; levothyroxine 75mcg OD. No anticoagulant or antiplatelet. Not on bone protection.
ALLERGIES: penicillin - rash.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in a ground-floor flat, independent, no falls in the last year. Non-smoker. Minimal alcohol. Daughter lives nearby.

ON EXAMINATION
Obs: HR 86, BP 144/82, RR 16,
  SpO2 97% on air, temp 36.6C. NEWS 0.
  Alert and orientated, comfortable at rest post-analgesia.
Right upper limb: dorsal angulation of the distal forearm with the classic dinner-fork
  deformity. Swelling and tenderness over the distal radius and over the ulnar styloid.
  Skin intact, no wound, no tenting, no blistering - closed injury.
Neurovascular: radial pulse present, capillary refill <2s, hand warm and well perfused.
  Sensation intact in median, ulnar and radial nerve distributions, including normal
  sensation over the volar thumb and index finger. Able to flex and extend all fingers.
  No pain on passive finger extension. No features of acute carpal tunnel syndrome and
  no features of compartment syndrome.
Elbow and shoulder on the same side: no tenderness, full passive range, no deformity.
Systemic: chest clear, heart sounds normal, abdomen soft. No head injury. C-spine
  non-tender. No other bony tenderness on secondary survey.

IMAGING
Plain radiographs right wrist, AP and lateral, 18:00:
  Dorsally displaced, comminuted, intra-articular fracture of the distal radius with 26 degrees
  of dorsal tilt and approximately 5mm loss of radial height.
  Associated ulnar styloid fracture. No carpal fracture, no dislocation.

PROCEDURE IN ED
Manipulation under haematoma block, dorsal below-elbow backslab at 18:25.
Post-reduction radiographs: improved but not anatomical - residual dorsal tilt
12 degrees with persisting articular step. Reduction not held.
Neurovascular status unchanged after manipulation and after casting.

INVESTIGATIONS
Hb 127, WCC 8.4, platelets 254.
Na 139, K 4.2, urea 5.6, creatinine 78.
Group and save sent. ECG: sinus rhythm, no acute change.

IMPRESSION
1. Closed dorsally displaced, comminuted, intra-articular fracture of the right distal radius with
   ulnar styloid fracture, neurovascularly intact, unstable after closed reduction.
2. Fragility fracture in a 78y female - low-energy mechanical fall.
For open reduction and internal fixation, volar locking plate.

PLAN
1. Admit under Trauma & Orthopaedics. Consultant informed, listed for
   open reduction and internal fixation, volar locking plate on the 30/07/2026 trauma list.
2. Nil by mouth from midnight. IV fluids while fasting.
3. Elevate right upper limb in a Bradford sling. Backslab checked - not circumferential,
   not tight.
4. Hourly neurovascular observations overnight. Escalate immediately for increasing pain,
   pain on passive finger extension, altered sensation in the thumb or index finger, or
   loss of the radial pulse.
5. Analgesia: regular paracetamol and PRN oral morphine. Avoid NSAIDs given age and
   antihypertensive use.
6. Continue usual medications.
7. Pre-op: anaesthetic review, consent, mark the right arm. Group and save valid.
8. VTE risk assessment completed - mobile, mechanical prophylaxis; review chemical
   prophylaxis if mobility drops.
9. Fragility fracture pathway: bone profile and vitamin D, refer to the fracture liaison
   service for DXA and bone protection.
10. Falls assessment and lying/standing BP. Occupational therapy review re: coping at home
    alone with one arm before discharge.
